mission_3.prediction: Changing the repulsion strength from 0 to 1.30 changed how far the robot moved away from the robot turned away from the person before oscillating back to its original path, mainly looking at the constrained map but at 0 it was just a straight line no turns at all just regular path, at 1.30 it started to create these small little bumps. Changing the influence distance also determines if the robots needs to actually bounce at all or if it can just go straight ahead.
mission_3.comparison: The completed condition with the largest minimum_person_clearance_m for rrt  was social_1 with 1.7268. compared to it's baseline it was a very minor change with a 0.0001 increase, the person_space_s value stayed the same amongst both.  As for A* highest minimum_person_clearance_m was social_2 with 0.7719. compared to it's baseline the value increases and the personal_space_s value dropped from 1.8 to 0.  Having wider spacing did not cost more time nor distance with rrt just being faster in general as well as traveling a shorter distance while still maintaining a wide enough space away from the person.
mission_3.recommendation: Rrt should be the planner, status succeeded, condition can be either baseline or social_1 depending if saving a bit of time and distance is worth the 0.0001 clearance. Static-person trials do not show the possibilities of needing to reroute or stop if there were moving people an example being if a robot creates a path based on where humans are initially but then a human later walks into the robots path and stops there, now there's an issue of deciding whether continue waiting or creating another path.
